problems.form_value: 'It does not say whether that check came before or after random assignment, so no count at assignment is printed (150 or 153 were randomized).'
problems.source_says: The paper prints no count at assignment. It does not say when the attention check took place, and it reports no dropouts between assignment and the end of the task. It also reports five exclusions 'due to idea data logging issues' without naming the sample. So the text gives a floor (all 150 submitters were assigned and produced ideas, p. 12) but no ceiling, and '150 or 153' is an inference. The form-spec field note says to write 'randomized' only for a count the paper gives at assignment. n_randomized = null is right. Only the parenthetical goes beyond the text.
problems.quote: An additional three submitters were excluded for failing an initial attention check.
problems.locator: p. 10, Participants; p. 11, Submission Phase; p. 12, Occasions; form-spec.md, Field notes, 'Counts in prose'

problems.form_value: 'Evaluators are a separate sample of raters (N = 142, CloudResearch Connect). Six were excluded for an attention check and five for idea data logging issues (p. 10)'
problems.source_says: The sentence comes right after the evaluator description, so the six attention-check exclusions are evaluators (the submitter attention-check exclusions are given separately as three). The five 'idea data logging' exclusions share that sentence, but the paper calls them only 'participants' and never names their sample. The evaluator reading is the more natural one, but it is an inference from placement. If the five were submitters, more than 153 people could have been assigned, or fewer than 128 analyzed. Criterion 2 holds either way.
problems.quote: Six participants were excluded for failing an initial attention check and five participants were excluded due to idea data logging issues.

problems.form_value: 'For the remaining AI-arm participants, object trials without chat data were dropped (no AI use in 24 percent of low-agency and 38 percent of high-agency trials, p. 13)'
problems.source_says: The 24 and 38 percent are shares of all trials in each AI arm. The paper says the 22 complete exclusions resulted from dropping those trials, so the percentages include the trials of the 22 people who were excluded entirely. Placed after 'For the remaining AI-arm participants', they overstate the trials lost by the people who stayed in the analysis. The paper does not print that smaller share. This is a wording issue and changes no count of people.
problems.quote: Object trials from the high- and low-agency conditions were excluded if they did not include chat data. On the participant level this resulted in 12 participants in the high-agency condition and 10 participants in the low-agency condition
problems.locator: p. 13, Manipulation Checks; p. 14; p. 39, Treatment Noncompliance

confirmed.statement: (a) Submitters: N = 150 community college students in the San Francisco Bay Area who took part for research credits; age M = 25.1 (SD = 9.2); 72 percent female. The form's participants.quote is verbatim.
(a, c) The 150 is net of three submitters 'excluded for failing an initial attention check'. The paper calls it the 'final sample', against a preregistered target of N = 450.

(a, b) All 150 submitters were assigned and did the task. Assignment comes after consent, and 'Across conditions, submitters produced a total of n = 2,250 ideas', which is 150 people x 5 uses x 3 objects. The 2,250 counts ideas, and the form does not use it as a count of people.
confirmed.locator: p. 11, Submission Phase; p. 12, Occasions; p. 14, Data Structure

confirmed.statement: (c) 12 high-agency and 10 low-agency participants were 'completely excluded from the analysis' because they did not use the chatbot. Page 14 lists this as a deviation from the preregistration. No control-arm exclusion is reported. 150 - 22 = 128 is arithmetic, as the form says.
confirmed.locator: pp. 13-14, Manipulation Checks; p. 14, Statistical Approach; p. 39, Treatment Noncompliance

confirmed.statement: (a) The paper prints no analyzed total and no per-arm count anywhere: not in the main text, Figures 1-3, Tables A1-A3, or Appendices A and B. Figure 1 shows dots (apparently one per submitter) without counts. So n_randomized and n_analyzed = null at study and arm level follow form-spec rule 1, and counts_are = people is right.
(b) Unit counts stay out of the people fields: 1,709 ratings per model (Table A2) and 337 sampled ideas (Table A3) are recorded as n_units.
confirmed.locator: p. 35, Table A2; p. 36, Table A3

confirmed.statement: (b) Evaluators (N = 142, CloudResearch Connect; age M = 46.7, SD = 16.3) are a separate rater sample and were not randomized. The form does not count them toward criterion 2.

(c) Ideas never drawn for evaluation are dropped from the rating models. The authors write that noncompliance 'somewhat compromised the random assignment'. The form records the per-protocol analysis and does not call it intention-to-treat.

(e) Printed numbers show well over 50 people analyzed, without the subtraction. Table A3 has 337 observations with one sampled idea per participant per object, so at least 113 people entered that model. The four Appendix B prompt tests compare per-participant proportions between the AI arms, and all report t(79) despite unequal SDs. That fits a pooled-variance test with 81 AI-arm people. The Tukey contrasts report t(125) and t(122). These are derived bounds, not printed counts.
confirmed.locator: p. 15, Homogeneity; p. 36, Table A3; pp. 41-42, Appendix B; p. 16, Homogeneity

confirmed.statement: (d) The paper reports one experiment. No passage says these submitters or evaluators appear in another paper, and candidates.json holds no other paper by these authors, so the empty sample_overlap is consistent. The ACM Creativity & Cognition 2026 version of record reports the same experiment, and source.version names it.
confirmed.locator: full text, pp. 1-42; candidates.json; retrieval.json entry c132

confirmed.statement: population = students, country = United States ('adult participants from the U.S.'), and the Research Experience Program locator in participants.who are right.

summary: Every count in the form checks out: 150 submitters were assigned and finished the task, 22 AI-arm noncompliers were dropped entirely, the paper prints no analyzed or per-arm count (so the nulls are right), and printed numbers (337 one-idea-per-person-per-object observations in Table A3, and per-participant t(79) tests in Appendix B) show well over 50 people analyzed in the single study. The coding fails only on three details in participants.exclusions: the text does not support '150 or 153 were randomized', the five 'idea data logging' exclusions are placed with the evaluators only by inference, and the 24 and 38 percent trial shares include the trials of the 22 people who were excluded entirely.
